title: Combination Sum
prompt:
Given **distinct** positive `candidates` and a `target`, return all unique combinations whose values sum to `target`. The **same number may be used any number of times**. Two combinations are the same if they use each number the same number of times.

**Example**: `candidates = [2,3,6,7]`, `target = 7` → `[[2,2,3],[7]]`.

**Constraints**: 1 ≤ candidates ≤ 30, 2 ≤ candidates[i] ≤ 40, 1 ≤ target ≤ 40.
hints: Build a combination one number at a time while tracking how much of the target is left. How do you allow a number to be picked again, without also producing [2,3,2] alongside [2,2,3]?
Backtrack with `(start, remaining)`: record a copy when `remaining == 0`; stop when it goes negative; loop `i` from `start`.
Recurse with `i`, not `i + 1`, so `candidates[i]` can repeat: `backtrack(i, remaining - candidates[i], ...)`.

solution.explanation: Recursing on `i` means "this number may be chosen again," while `start` keeps choices in non-decreasing index order, so reordered duplicates never appear. Negative remainders end a branch right away. Time is exponential, roughly O(n^(target/min)) branches in the worst case; the recursion depth is at most target/min.
